finding.statement: The current JSPACE_VECTOR_CONTROL_ABI/v1 packet builds target_model_runtime_identity from the measured source PyTorch runtime/checkpoint/tokenizer identity and target_activation_site from the source intervention. That is valid for the existing same-runtime loopback candidate, but it cannot truthfully establish the next requested Qwen3-0.6B GGUF + llama.cpp native cvec target. Copying those source identities into a native target would collapse source component evidence into false target provenance.
finding.counterhypothesis: The PyTorch and native targets may implement equivalent vector semantics, but equivalence is not established by model family/name, equal vector dimension, or a source-runtime PASS. It requires an explicit target runtime/artifact/vector/layer binding and later native consumption receipt.
finding.falsifier: A native target binding is admissible only if the existing source control packet is hash-valid and same-runtime, the target runtime identity differs explicitly, the exact source vector is named, llama_set_adapter_cvec is the declared native API, dimensions match without silent projection, and a deterministic target-layer mapping/conversion receipt is present. Runtime credit remains false until later exact execution consumes the binding.
